As defined (only Jacobson's formula for (x+y)^[p]) the notion is too weak: on the abelian Lie algebra k the identity satisfies it but is not a restricted structure when some c has c^p ≠ c (id_not_restricted). The axioms (λx)^[p] = λ^p x^[p] and ad(x^[p]) = (ad x)^p were added. Probably an oral abbreviation of the lecture. The Lean definition RestrictedLie is the equivalent "faithful representation with x^[p] ↦ x^p" form (restricted PBW, not proved).

correction.old: A restricted Lie algebra is a Lie algebra in characteristic $p$ with a map $x\mapsto x^{[p]}$ such that $(x+y)^{[p]}-x^{[p]}-y^{[p]}$ is given by Jacobson's formula, a Lie polynomial in $x,y$.
correction.new: A restricted Lie algebra is a Lie algebra in characteristic $p$ with a map $x\mapsto x^{[p]}$ such that $(\lambda x)^{[p]}=\lambda^px^{[p]}$, $\mathrm{ad}(x^{[p]})=(\mathrm{ad}\,x)^p$ and $(x+y)^{[p]}-x^{[p]}-y^{[p]}$ is given by Jacobson's formula, a Lie polynomial in $x,y$.

note: The p-th power of a derivation is a derivation (Leibniz formula and p | C(p,i)). Lie(G) as left-invariant derivations / ε-derivations of the Hopf algebra is not built.
The ideal of G₁ = ker F (generated by a^p, a ∈ m) lies in m², so m/m² — whose dual is Lie(G) — is the same for G and G₁. The identification Lie(G) = (m/m²)* is not restated.
